input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: an optional argument's metavar is wrapped in brackets without checking whether the type already bracketed it
- failure path: an optional Choice argument renders in the usage line as [[foo|bar|baz]] with two pairs of brackets instead of [foo|bar|baz]

Reviewer finding
- description: Removing the already_bracketed check means optional parameters whose metavar already starts and ends with brackets get wrapped in brackets a second time, producing malformed usage text such as [[a|b]].
- rationale: Trigger: an optional click.Option with a Choice type, whose get_metavar returns a bracketed string like [a|b], or a user-supplied metavar such as [VALUE]. Mechanism: the condition is now only not self.required, so f"[{var}]" wraps the already-bracketed var again. Impact: --help and usage output show doubled brackets, a visible regression from the previous behavior that this check existed to prevent.
critique: The finding describes the same mechanism as the label: an optional argument's metavar gets wrapped in brackets without checking whether it is already bracketed. It also gives the same failure, an optional Choice rendering as [[a|b]].
